newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Huta Katowice denies Thai dumping charges.
newsitem.headline: Polish Huta Katowice denies Thai dumping charges.

text.p: The largest Polish steel mill, Huta Katowice SA, denies charges made by Thai officals that it was dumping steel and will apply for arbitration to the World Trade Organization (WTO), a mill spokeswoman said.
"Huta Katowice already has gathered all the materials and of course we will appeal against Thailand's charges," Renata Bytomska told Reuters on Wednesday.
Bytomska said however that before any steps were taken by Huta Katowice, the mill must be officially notified by Thailand about the implementation of the country's special anti-dumping duties.
She said Thailand imposed one rate of anti-dumping tariff on H-beam imports from Poland at 27.78 percent in late May.
Previously Thailand levied a 25.90 percent duty on imports from Poland's Huta Katowice.

Thai companies have claimed that Polish structural steel costs about $500 dollars per tonne in Poland but only $265 per tonne when exported to Thailand, but Bytomska said that these prices refer to two different products.
Huta Katowice has been exporting its products to Thailand since the early 1990s and the value of its exports to the country in 1996 amounted to $40 million.
